correctness.rationale: The independent-innovations factorization proves the exact Ornstein–Uhlenbeck precision quadratic form. A single adjacent gap \(\delta\) produces a divergent eigenvalue \(1/(\gamma\delta)+O(1)\); the probability of multiple near-collisions is lower order after the auxiliary cutoff is removed. Independent-density convolution gives collision intensity \(n(n-1)\int w(x)^2\,dx\). Layer-cake and Stieltjes integration then give the sharp \(q<1\) moment boundary, the nugget logarithmic coefficient and the \(q>1\) coefficient \(C_{n,w,\gamma}/(q-1)\). The checker tests exact rational identities and finite diagnostics; infinite claims rest on analytical proofs.

value.rationale: Near-coincident random sample locations produce ill-conditioned Gaussian-process covariance systems. The exact \(1/t\) tail normalization quantifies rather than merely asserts the problem, the sampling-density functional \(\int w^2\) gives a sharp design comparison, and explicit regularized expected-norm blow-ups quantify the numerical cost of removing jitter. These are motivated numerical linear-algebra facts, not arbitrary one-off computations.
